title: Ansible for networking: inventory, vendor modules and idempotency

videos.script: Ansible is the tool most network teams reach for first. You do not write a program. You describe what the network should look like, in YAML, and Ansible works out what to run. {{describe}} An inventory says which devices exist and how they are grouped. Variables beside it say what makes each one different. {{inventory}} A playbook says what every router should have. You run it, and each router reports changed or ok. Run it again, and every router says ok, because there is nothing left to do. {{idempotent}} In this lesson you configure BGP on three routers from one playbook, with each router's own values, and check that every session comes up. {{bgp}} Then the parts that bite. A secret has to be in the repository without being readable. And a task has to tell the truth about whether it changed something. {{secrets}}
